f1.quote: compared AlCoCrFeNi2.1 with DS2205 after three rapid heating/quenching cycles to approximately 1100 °C

f2.quote: immersed reciprocating ball-on-flat tribo-corrosion against a 6.35 mm alumina ball. Sliding lasted 1800 s after 3600 s of open-circuit-potential stabilization; load was varied from 5 to 15 N and frequency from 3 to 9 Hz.

f3.quote: Tribo-corrosion was conducted in 100 mL deionized water at 25, 50, and 100 °C with a 3.5 mm stroke

f4.quote: Sliding lasted 1800 s after 3600 s of open-circuit-potential stabilization

f5.quote: the principal temperature comparison used 5 N and 5 Hz. Samples remained immersed for 300 s after sliding to monitor repassivation. Tests at 100 °C used a covered cell and reflux condenser.

f6.quote: Near 50 °C, faster film repair without extensive brittle-film disruption produces a low-shear, polishing regime and minimizes wear.

f7.quote: At 100 °C, repeated oxide/tribo-layer formation, fracture, and removal causes oxidative or third-body wear and greater friction instability.

f8.quote: The HEA retained its fine L12/B2 lamellar structure after thermal shock and supported comparatively homogeneous Cr availability, robust passive-film repair

f9.quote: Relative to DS2205 under identical conditions, AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is expected to retain its phase structure better and exhibit more stable passivation, lower coefficient of friction, smaller wear volume, and substantially lower tribo-corrosion wear rate.

f10.quote: The HEA retained its fine L12/B2 lamellar structure after thermal shock

f12.quote: For both alloys, degradation is expected to be minimized near 50 °C rather than at 25 or 100 °C.
